block-file-and-object-storage.r: A report job went from ten minutes to two hours after a move to a cheaper volume. The new volume was a throughput HDD type, but the database did small random reads and the disk sat at 99.8 percent busy. An SSD volume fixed it.
block-file-and-object-storage.x: Match the volume to the access pattern. Check IOPS and latency limits in the provider's volume types, watch await and utilization with iostat, and test with fio on a scratch volume of the same type before migrating.

filesystems-ext4-xfs-and-mounts.r: A server stayed in emergency mode after a reboot because a UUID in fstab was typed with one character missing and the line had no nofail. The team now copies UUIDs from blkid, adds nofail and runs mount -a before leaving.
filesystems-ext4-xfs-and-mounts.x: Treat fstab as boot-critical code: review it, use UUIDs, nofail for non-root data, and test with mount -a. Monitor inode use beside byte use, and keep a console or rescue path for the day a mount blocks boot.

lvm-and-raid.r: A RAID 5 array lost a second disk while rebuilding. The first failure was a week old and its alert went to a mailbox nobody read. The team restored from backup and rebuilt as RAID 6 with working alerts.
lvm-and-raid.x: Redundancy is only as good as the time to notice and repair. Alert on degraded state, keep hot spares, size rebuild windows for the disk size, prefer double parity or mirrors for large disks, and keep backups on separate systems.

network-storage-nfs-iscsi-and-ceph.r: Rebooting one NFS server hung thirty application servers because their mounts were hard, and even df hung monitoring. Service resumed after twelve minutes. The team made the exports highly available and put timeouts on checks.
network-storage-nfs-iscsi-and-ceph.x: Every network mount is a dependency that can hang a host. Make storage servers redundant, put timeouts in monitoring and scripts, use multipath for block access, and watch Ceph capacity and degraded placement groups.

performance-backups-and-troubleshooting.r: A disk alert fired at 100 percent but du found only 3.4 GB. A rotated log file had been deleted while the Java process kept writing, and it held 44 GB. Restarting the service freed the space and rotation was fixed with copytruncate.
performance-backups-and-troubleshooting.x: Work in order: device, mount, space and inodes, then latency. Reconcile df and du, find deleted-but-open files, size backups by RPO and RTO, keep an immutable copy off-site, and schedule restore drills.

backup-and-dr-strategy-3-2-1-and-retenti.r: After an administrator's credentials were stolen, the attacker deleted a production database and its backups, which lived in the same account. Recovery used a six-week-old export from a partner. Backups moved to a separate account with object lock.
backup-and-dr-strategy-3-2-1-and-retenti.x: Replication is not backup, because deletions replicate too. Separate the credentials that can delete production from those that can delete backups, and test restores regularly.

backup-and-dr-database-backups-and-point.r: During a recovery drill the newest archived WAL segment was nine weeks old. A rotated credential had broken archive_command, and nobody had alerts. After fixing it the team added alerts on archive failure and a quarterly restore drill.
backup-and-dr-database-backups-and-point.x: Point-in-time recovery turns hours of loss into seconds, but only if archiving works. Monitor pg_stat_archiver and practice recovery to a timestamp before you need it.

backup-and-dr-kubernetes-etcd-and-volume.r: A team restored a volume snapshot of a database after a failed upgrade. The snapshot was taken during writes, so recovery replayed a long log and some recent transactions were lost. Native database backups with log archiving became the main path.
backup-and-dr-kubernetes-etcd-and-volume.x: Know what each backup can restore. A storage snapshot is crash-consistent, not application-consistent, and a snapshot in the same storage is not a disaster recovery copy.

backup-and-dr-testing-restores-and-verif.r: When a file server failed, the team found nightly backups had been empty for nine months after a path change, while the log said completed successfully. A size baseline check, weekly restore test and a last-tested-restore dashboard now cover every system.
backup-and-dr-testing-restores-and-verif.x: Job success proves little. Run restore tests with row counts and latest timestamps, measure how long they take, and treat a failed or missing backup as an incident.

backup-and-dr-disaster-recovery-patterns.r: When a region failed, the standby started but ran out of capacity within minutes: it had four nodes against thirty-six, and a launch quota nobody had raised. The service was degraded for ninety minutes. Quotas and load tests of the DR site followed.
backup-and-dr-disaster-recovery-patterns.x: Data is the hard part. Check capacity and quotas at the DR site, keep it in step with production through code, and agree the failover decision rule in advance to avoid split-brain.

backup-and-dr-ransomware-immutable-backu.r: After a ransomware attack a company restored its servers within a day, and they were encrypted again two hours later. The attacker's service account and a scheduled task were still in place. The new runbook contains and rotates first, then restores.
backup-and-dr-ransomware-immutable-backu.x: Assume an administrator account can be compromised. Restoring into an environment that is still compromised wastes the backup, so rebuild identity, rotate credentials and restore from a clean point.

storage-benchmarking-with-fio.r: A volume looked fast in a sequential test but a database on it was slow. A random 4k test at realistic queue depth showed high latency, and the team changed the volume type.
storage-benchmarking-with-fio.x: Benchmark the workload, not the hardware's brochure. The right test is short, repeatable and run where it cannot damage data.
